candidates.snippet: Streetlights by Operational Status - Updated weekly
candidates.source_description: The Streetlights Status Dashboard visualizes streetlight data sourced weekly from the City's service vendor, Dalkia, with periodic updates from PNM. The Department of Municipal Development (DMD) is currently working on a data-sharing agreement with PNM to integrate additional work order information. This dashboard is embedded on the City’s website and is optimized for the current calendar year—widget configurations will be updated annually as needed. As it is frequently accessed via mobile devices, the dashboard should be periodically reviewed to ensure proper functionality and formatting.

candidates.snippet: Current bikeways and trails infrastructure data for the City of Albuquerque.
candidates.source_description: This dataset represents the most up-to-date bikeways and trails infrastructure within the City of Albuquerque. It is a dynamic, actively maintained layer that reflects changes and additions to the network as they occur. This differs from the "Existing Infrastructure" layer found in the 2024 Bikeways and Trails Facility Plan dataset, which provides a static snapshot of the network at the time of the plan’s development. Users seeking a historical reference of facilities used during the planning process should refer to that dataset. This layer, by contrast, supports real-time applications, current infrastructure planning, and public information. Path Types: Bike Lane - A portion of the street with a designated lane for bicycles. Buffered Bike Lane - Conventional bike lanes paired with a designated buffer space to provide separation from motorized traffic. Separated Bike Lane - A bike lane that is physically separated from motor vehicle traffic with a vertical element (barrier). Paved Multi-Use Trail - A paved trail closed to automotive traffic and separated from the roadway system. Paved Sidepath - A paved trail and/or sidewalk closed to motor vehicle traffic and parallel to a roadway. Bike Blvd. - A shared roadway optimized by bicycle traffic. Bike Route - Cars and bicycles share the road. Signs and markings may be present. Unpaved Multi-Use Trail – An unpaved trail closed to automotive traffic. Hiking Trail - An unpaved trail open to foot traffic only. Crossing - Bicycle or pedestrian under/over crossings. Deprecated Types: NMDOT Facility - A Bicycle facility owned and maintained by NMDOT with different design standards than the City of Albuquerque.

candidates.anchor_text: City of Albuquerque School Crossings Dashboard
candidates.snippet: Safety ratings for school crossings in CABQ
candidates.source_description: This dashboard provides information about over 350 school crossings in the City of Albuquerque. Data is shown based on the crossing score and rating system developed during this evaluation. Tools are available to select particular schools, areas, and crossing features as well as sorting by rating. Crossing ratings were updated in 2024 and will continue to be updated as needed. School locations and Walk Zones were provided by Albuquerque Public Schools and were last updated in 2022 with updated Walk Zone data expected in 2025.

candidates.snippet: Restrooms located at city-operated facilities that are open for public use. This layer includes each restroom’s address and hours of operation, covering both current and planned future locations. It supports the Public Restroom Finder Web App on the City's website.
candidates.source_description: This dataset was originally compiled from a spreadsheet provided by the City's Executive Operations Officer and is regularly updated. Each point represents a publicly accessible restroom at a city-operated facility. The "Department" field uses acronyms to indicate the department responsible for maintenance of the associated location. The original data included fields for general weekday hours ("Hours M–F") and specific day exceptions ("Specific Day Exceptions"). An initial script was used to standardize daily hours across the week to support the web app's pop-up display functionality. The "Notes" field contains additional context such as seasonal availability or other relevant public information displayed in the application's pop-ups.
